capitals.note: 'Stanwick was excavated by Wheeler, who thought Venutius likely held it as his capital. Later Durham excavations suggested it was a centre of power for Cartimandua instead.' The page gives Isurium Brigantum (Aldborough, 54.09 N 1.40 W) as the Roman-era capital. The coordinates are the village's; the page gives none.

rulers.title: client queen
rulers.note: The lead dates her reign from c. AD 43 ('uncertain'); the infobox says 'before AD 51 - AD 69'; evacuated in 69, 'leaving Venutius in control'.

rulers.name: Venutius
rulers.title: king (after the 69 revolt)
rulers.note: Her husband and then rival; invaded her kingdom in 52-57 and again in 69; the end of his rule is not on the pages (bridged to the end of Cerialis's governorship). Vellocatus, her armour-bearer and second consort, was 'raised to kingship' (Brigantes page, undated).

ledger.note: c. 43: the Brigantes' kingdom under Cartimandua. Cartimandua page: the lead has her 'reigned c. AD 43 - c. 69', the infobox 'before AD 51 - AD 69'; 'her rule over the Brigantes may already have been established' when Claudius began the conquest in 43, and 'she may have been one of the eleven "kings"' who surrendered to Claudius without a fight; Tacitus first mentions her in 51, when she handed Caratacus over in chains. The Roman conquest of Britain page: 'the Roman client tribe of the Brigantes'. The Brigantes page has Ostorius Scapula forced in 47 to abandon his campaign because of 'disaffection' among the Brigantes. The pages describe no treaty. 'Venutius staged another revolt, again with help from other nations'; Rome could send only auxiliaries, and 'Cartimandua was evacuated, leaving Venutius in control of a kingdom at war with Rome' (Cartimandua page). The roman-empire dossier should carry the mirror (vassal_end, counterpart brigantes, 69). [Fix 2026-10-19, reviewer eu-04-x.]

69: Venutius takes over. 'Venutius staged another rebellion in 69, taking advantage of Roman instability in the Year of the Four Emperors'; Rome 'could only send auxiliaries, and Cartimandua was evacuated, leaving Venutius in control'. He had invaded her kingdom in 52-57 and Roman cohorts defended her until Caesius Nasica arrived with legion IX Hispana. The state and its land continue under Venutius, no longer a Roman client.

wars.name: Venutius's revolts against Cartimandua
wars.outcome: Venutius invaded her kingdom during Didius Gallus's governorship (52-57); in 57 Roman cohorts and then Caesius Nasica with legion IX Hispana defeated the rebels; he rebelled again with a faction and then in 69, when Cartimandua was evacuated and Venutius took control.
wars.note: A civil war inside the client kingdom, with Roman support to the queen.
